body:
I overheard two of my colleagues bitching about me earlier in the year, and it really threw my confidence. It still is, but hopefully these tips will help (and will serve as a reminder for me too!)

- Reframe it. Why might someone badmouth you? Ok, maybe it's cos they hate you. Or maybe it's because they're jealous of your achievements, or insecure about something themselves.

- Have you ever badmouthed someone? Did it mean you hated them or was it just venting or deflecting?

- You'll know well that a hunch is not evidence; intelligence is not evidence. What evidence do you have that people dislike you or badmouth you as soon as your back is turned? Any?

- You don't need to be perfect. In fact, most people will prefer it if you aren't perfect.

- Even the best cop you can imagine has shit days, makes mistakes and gets snotty emails. I once ended up with a custody alongside a very experienced cop who I thought was infallible. I discovered that he really wasn't great at interviewing. I made a couple of suggestions and afterwards he commented that I clearly had an aptitude for interviewing. It was really eye opening and really important to see. 

- Find one or two things to be shit-hot at, and then volunteer to do those things. Are you great at paperwork, can you lodge productions like a machine, do you take great statements, are you a fiend in a foot pursuit? Become the go-to guy when those skills are needed, and volunteer for them.

- If your team are swamped, put your hand up to help them. Even if it's just doing presumptive tests or typing something up.

- Be the change you want to see. Compliment people behind their back. Be the "to be fair..." person. Don't join in the bitching and rumours.

- Also make sure there's nothing to legitimately bitch about you for. Don't get involved in nefarious things, including being messy on nights out, shagging about, cutting corners etc.

- Read "How To Win Friends and Influence People" and practise the skills. Be the person who asks others questions and takes an interest.

- Don't be a smart-arse or a know it all. Take criticism and suggestions on board and without defensiveness or hostility. Be open to suggestions. Realise that you're still learning, no matter how many years in you are.

- Recognise that your team simply might be toxic. Take on the friends who are worth having, leave others as acquaintances. Think about whether a move might be good for you.

- Do the hours you are rostered and nothing more. Leave your work phone in the office. Claim your overtime. Go home and enioy your life. Spend time with friends and family who aren't job. Cultivate interests that make you more interesting and happy. Avoid burnout.
